requirement_text.REQ-419:
Build-order M1 (docs/mobile/build-order.md): MOB-1 in docs/mobile/requirements.md, placement and stack per docs/mobile/architecture.md §2, stack settled by docs/migration/decisions/0012-mobile-tier-stack.md (not re-decided here). This requirement creates apps/mobile/; nothing in it authenticates or fetches (that is REQ-421).

BUILDS:
1. `flutter create --org com.bizdala --project-name letflow --platforms android,ios apps/mobile` (Android applicationId and iOS bundle id com.bizdala.letflow -- must match REQ-418's redirect scheme). Android minSdk 26 in android/app/build.gradle(.kts); iOS deployment target 15.0 in ios/Podfile and the Xcode project.
2. pubspec.yaml: environment pins `sdk` to the Dart 3.11 line and a `flutter: 3.41.7` constraint (REQ-420's CI reads the Flutter version from this file); dependencies go_router, flutter_riverpod, dio, flutter_appauth, flutter_secure_storage, intl -- nothing else at runtime yet (the local cache store is REQ-423's choice).
3. lib/ layout exactly per architecture.md §2 (bootstrap/, auth/, api/, definitions/, renderers/{form,list,process,task}/, features/, design_system/, i18n/, shared/), a ProviderScope root, and a go_router with a placeholder slug-entry route. A renderer registry in lib/renderers/ keyed by definition type that returns an explicit "unsupported definition type" widget for an unknown type -- never a blank screen (MOB-4's stale-version principle, applied from day one).
4. analysis_options.yaml including flutter_lints (or stricter).
5. THREE STATIC GUARDS as ordinary Dart tests under apps/mobile/test/guards/ (so they run in `flutter test` and fail CI, not warn; architecture.md §6 requires the boundary rule to fail the build):
(a) module boundary, 0039 D3 as restated in architecture.md §6: no file outside lib/features/<id>/ imports from it except the one sanctioned navigation-bootstrap file, and lib/features/a/ imports from lib/features/b/ only if b is in a's declared depends_on (store the declaration in a single Dart/JSON manifest the guard reads);
(b) forbidden dependencies: pubspec.yaml and pubspec.lock contain no script runtime (e.g. flutter_js, any lua or wasm runtime package), no CEL package (REQ-294 forbids one), and no webview package (webview_flutter, flutter_inappwebview -- MOB-2 forbids embedded webview OIDC);
(c) no tenant identifier compiled in: no string literal in lib/ equals a tenant slug or realm name that exists in priv/keycloak/realms/*.json or test/support fixtures (at minimum 'bpm-default'), and no asset under apps/mobile/assets/ is tenant-specific.
Each guard must include a self-test proving it fires (e.g. runs its checker over an in-test fixture string that violates it).
6. apps/mobile/README.md: how to run (`flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`, `flutter run -d emulator-5554`), the platform API base URL supplied at build time via --dart-define=LETFLOW_API_BASE_URL (a platform endpoint per environment, not a tenant identifier), and how to reach a local backend from the emulator: `adb reverse tcp:<api-port> tcp:<api-port>` and `adb reverse tcp:<keycloak-port> tcp:<keycloak-port>` so the device reaches both at localhost. State why 10.0.2.2 is not enough: it reaches the API, but Keycloak stamps a token's iss from the host the browser used, so a login through 10.0.2.2 yields an iss the backend's configured issuer (localhost) rejects. Update docs/mobile/README.md's "Nothing is built" line to state the scaffold exists as of this requirement.

iOS: files are generated and configured; building them is DEFERRED -- the build host is Windows and cannot run Xcode. Recorded, not dropped.

result.summary:
Built apps/mobile/ exactly per lib/letflow/design/req419-mobile-scaffold.md. flutter create --org com.bizdala --project-name letflow --platforms android,ios apps/mobile, then hand-authored: lib/ tree (bootstrap/, auth/, api/, definitions/, renderers/{form,list,process,task}/, features/, design_system/, i18n/, shared/, main.dart, app.dart), renderer_registry.dart with UnsupportedDefinitionTypeWidget fallback, analysis_options.yaml (flutter_lints, unmodified), the three static guards under test/guards/ each with a real-tree test + a self-test on a violating fixture, a widget test on the renderer fallback, README.md updates in both apps/mobile/ and docs/mobile/, and ios/Podfile with platform :ios, '15.0' (uncommented from the stock Flutter cocoapods template) plus IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET bumped to 15.0 in all 3 project.pbxproj build-config blocks. Android build.gradle.kts: minSdk pinned to literal 26, applicationId com.bizdala.letflow (flutter create's own org+name convention). pubspec.yaml: environment sdk >=3.11.0 <3.12.0 / flutter 3.41.7, dependencies added via `flutter pub add go_router flutter_riverpod dio flutter_appauth flutter_secure_storage intl` (resolved versions: go_router 17.5.0, flutter_riverpod 2.6.1, dio 5.11.1, flutter_appauth 12.1.0, flutter_secure_storage 11.2.0, intl 0.20.3) -- no other runtime dependency; stock cupertino_icons was auto-removed by pub. Deleted the stock counter-app test/widget_test.dart (didn't compile against the new app.dart shape) in favor of the guard tests + the renderer-fallback widget test, per the design's open question 3.

One build fix beyond the design doc's text: `flutter build apk --debug` failed on first attempt with 'Attribute data@scheme at AndroidManifest.xml requires a placeholder substitution but no value for <appAuthRedirectScheme> is provided' -- flutter_appauth's own AndroidManifest.xml declares a redirect intent-filter placeholder that must resolve to the app's custom scheme. Added `manifestPlaceholders["appAuthRedirectScheme"] = "com.bizdala.letflow"` to android/app/build.gradle.kts's defaultConfig. This is app-identity wiring only (the same identifier already fixed by REQ-418's Keycloak client registration and this requirement's own applicationId) -- no auth logic, no fetch, nothing beyond what's needed for the dependency's manifest merge to succeed.
